documents.title: H&P - Admission, Community-Acquired Pneumonia
lines: ADMISSION HISTORY AND PHYSICAL
Time of eval: 21:40, ED bay 7
Chief complaint: cough and fever x 4 days, worsening breathlessness today
HPI:
74 yo male, former smoker, presents with productive cough of rust-colored sputum, subjective fevers, pleuritic right-sided chest pain.
Onset 4 days ago with dry cough and myalgias; sputum became purulent 2 days ago.
Today developed dyspnea walking from bedroom to kitchen, plus 3 episodes of non-bloody vomiting.
Denies hemoptysis. No leg swelling. No recent travel. No sick contacts known.
Vomiting has limited PO intake to sips of water since this morning.
No chest pressure at rest, no orthopnea, no PND.
Past Medical History:
Hypertension
Type 2 diabetes mellitus, diet and metformin controlled
Osteoarthritis, both knees
Benign prostatic hyperplasia
Home Medications:
amlodipine 5 mg PO daily
lisinopril 20 mg PO daily
metformin 500 mg PO BID
tamsulosin 0.4 mg PO qHS
acetaminophen 500 mg PO PRN knee pain
Allergies: penicillin - childhood rash per pt (tolerates cephalosporins previously)
Social: lives with wife, independent in ADLs, walks 2 blocks daily without stopping. Quit cigarettes 18 yrs ago, 30 pack-yr. No alcohol.
Family Hx: father MI at 70, mother CVA.
Review of Systems:
Positive: fever, chills, cough, sputum, dyspnea, pleuritic pain, nausea, vomiting, poor appetite.
Negative: no dysuria, no diarrhea, no rash, no syncope. Pt alert and fully oriented, answers all history questions himself.
Physical Exam:
Vitals at triage: T 38.9 C, HR 104, BP 138/78, respiratory rate 32, SpO2 93% on RA.
Repeat vitals at 4 hours: T 38.4 C, HR 98, BP 132/74, respiratory rate 30, SpO2 92% on RA.
Gen: ill-appearing, diaphoretic, speaking in short phrases.
HEENT: dry mucous membranes, no JVD.
Cardiac: tachycardic, regular, no murmur, no rub.
Lungs: dullness to percussion right base, crackles right mid and lower zones, egophony right axilla. No wheeze. Accessory muscle use present.
Abd: soft, nontender, BS present.
Ext: no edema, warm, cap refill brisk.
Neuro: nonfocal, follows all commands, GCS 15.
Labs on arrival:
WBC 16.4 K with 88% neutrophils, Hgb 13.1, Plt 244
Na 127 mEq/L, K 4.2, Cl 94, HCO3 22, BUN 34 mg/dL, Cr 1.3, glucose 168
Lactate 1.9, CRP 188, procalcitonin 2.6
Blood cultures x2 drawn 21:15. Sputum gram stain and culture sent. Resp viral panel pending.
Imaging:
Chest x-ray (portable, 21:05): right lower and right middle lobe infiltrate with small right pleural effusion. No pneumothorax. Heart size normal.
Assessment:

74 yo male with community-acquired pneumonia, right middle and lower lobe, with small ipsilateral effusion. CURB-65 of 3 (age >=65, elevated BUN, respiratory rate >=30) - admit to medicine, telemetry bed.
Hyponatremia Na 127, likely SIADH from pneumonia vs poor intake.
Mild renal impairment, likely prerenal from vomiting and insensible losses.
Plan:
Ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily started 22:00; add IV azithromycin 500 mg daily. Antibiotics per severe CAP pathway, IV route given vomiting.
Ondansetron 4 mg IV q6h PRN; hold metformin while NPO/vomiting.
Titrate O2 to keep SpO2 >=92%; RT to assess q shift.
Incentive spirometer q1h while awake, encourage mobility with RN assist.
Hold lisinopril pending renal function and Na trend.
Monitor Na q12h; trend BUN/Cr daily.
Repeat CXR or bedside US if effusion enlarges or O2 need rises.
CBG checks q6h while off metformin.
Discussed with wife at bedside; questions answered. Attending notified 22:20.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Morning
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2, 07:35
Subjective: Pt reports cough looser overnight, still pleuritic pain with deep breath. Vomited twice overnight, most recently 03:50. No PO intake tolerated.
Overnight events: 1L NC placed overnight for SpO2 91% while sleeping; weaned to RA at 06:30 with SpO2 94%.
Slept in 30 degree upright position. No fevers after 02:00.
Vitals: T max 38.2 C at 00:40, T 37.4 C now. HR 92. BP 136/80. RR 24. SpO2 94% on RA at rest.
Intake/output: PO minimal, IV maintenance only, UOP 1050 mL/24h.
Exam:
Gen: appears more comfortable, speaking full sentences.
Lungs: crackles persist right base and right axilla, dullness right base unchanged. No new wheeze.
Cardiac: RRR, no murmur.
Abd: soft, nontender.
Neuro: alert, oriented x3, no deficits.
Labs this AM: WBC 13.8, Na 129, K 4.0, BUN 30, Cr 1.1, glucose 154.
Blood cultures NGTD at 10 hours. Sputum culture: mixed respiratory flora, prelim. Resp viral panel negative.
Assessment/Plan:

1. Severe CAP, RML/RLL with small right effusion - continue ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily and IV azithromycin. No change today. Continue IV route as pt unable to tolerate oral intake due to vomiting through day 2.
2. Hypoxemia - trend improving. Keep SpO2 >=92%, use 1L NC overnight PRN with sleep.
3. Nausea/vomiting - scheduled ondansetron 4 mg IV q8h instead of PRN; clear liquid trial at noon.
4. Hyponatremia - Na up to 129. Continue q12h Na. Lisinopril remains on hold.
5. Renal - Cr improved to 1.1, metformin still held.
6. Pain - acetaminophen 650 mg IV q6h PRN pleuritic pain.
7. Mobility - out of bed to chair TID, incentive spirometer q1h awake.
8. Dispo - likely 2 more inpatient days pending PO tolerance and O2 wean.
Discussed plan with pt and daughter by phone 08:10.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD3
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD3, 08:05
Subjective: Pt states he feels 'much better'. No vomiting since 03:50 yesterday. Ate half of breakfast tray and kept it down. Cough less frequent, sputum now light yellow.
Ambulated hallway x2 with RN yesterday evening, no dyspnea at rest.
Overnight events: no O2 required overnight, SpO2 93-95% on RA on continuous monitor. No fevers x 30 hours.
Vitals: T 36.9 C, HR 80, BP 128/76, RR 18, SpO2 95% on RA ambulating.
I/O: PO 900 mL, UOP 1600 mL.
Exam:
Gen: sitting up in chair, comfortable, no accessory muscle use.
Lungs: scattered crackles right base only, right mid zone clearing, no dullness change.
Cardiac: RRR.
Abd: soft, bowel sounds normal, no tenderness.
Ext: no edema.
Neuro: alert, fully oriented, steady gait with single-person standby.
Labs: WBC 9.6, Hgb 12.8, Na 133, K 4.1, BUN 21, Cr 1.0, glucose 141.
Blood cultures x2 no growth at 34 hours. Sputum culture final: normal respiratory flora.
Assessment/Plan:

1. CAP, RML/RLL with small right pleural effusion - clinically improving. Effusion small and not loculated; no thoracentesis indicated. Now tolerating PO - transition antibiotics to oral respiratory agent today, plan total 5 day course.
2. Last dose of ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily given 10:00 yesterday; IV azithromycin transitioned to oral azithromycin 500 mg PO daily this AM.
3. Oxygenation - off supplemental O2 >24 h, maintains SpO2 >=93% with ambulation. Continue pulse ox with activity.
4. Hyponatremia - Na 133, correcting appropriately with improved intake. Recheck tomorrow AM.
5. Renal - Cr 1.0, BUN down. Restart lisinopril 20 mg daily tomorrow if BP stable and Cr steady.
6. DM2 - resume metformin 500 mg BID now that eating; CBG 141.
7. Continue incentive spirometer, ambulate TID.
8. Dispo - anticipate discharge HD4 if stable overnight; wife able to provide home support.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Community-Acquired Pneumonia
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Discharge time: HD4, 13:20. Length of stay 4 days.
Admitting diagnosis: Community-acquired pneumonia, right middle and right lower lobe, with small right pleural effusion.
Discharge diagnoses: 1. CAP, resolving. 2. Hyponatremia, resolved. 3. Acute kidney injury from volume losses, resolved. 4. HTN. 5. Type 2 DM.
Brief Hospital Course:
74 yo male admitted with 4 days of cough, fever and pleuritic chest pain. At triage respiratory rate 32 and SpO2 93% on RA; respiratory rate 30 at 4 hours.
Admission labs notable for BUN 34 mg/dL, sodium 127 mEq/L on arrival, WBC 16.4.
Chest x-ray on arrival: right lower and right middle lobe infiltrate with small right pleural effusion.
CURB-65 of 3 documented in the admitting note; admitted to a monitored medicine bed.
Treated with ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily and IV azithromycin; unable to tolerate oral intake due to vomiting through day 2, so IV route maintained.
1L NC placed overnight for SpO2 91% while sleeping on HD1-2; weaned to room air HD2 morning and remained off O2 thereafter.
Nausea controlled with scheduled ondansetron; PO tolerated from HD3 and antibiotics converted to oral azithromycin to complete a 5 day total course.
Sodium corrected to 127 -> 129 -> 133 -> 136 with improved intake. Cr 1.3 on arrival, 0.9 at discharge.
Blood cultures x2 negative at 58 hours. Sputum culture normal respiratory flora. Respiratory viral panel negative.
Metformin and lisinopril held on admission, both resumed prior to discharge without issue.
Discharge Vitals: T 36.8 C, HR 76, BP 126/74, RR 18, SpO2 96% on RA, ambulating without desaturation.
Discharge Exam: comfortable, lungs with minimal residual crackles right base, no dullness change, abdomen benign, alert and fully oriented, gait steady.
Discharge Labs: WBC 8.2, Hgb 12.9, Na 136, K 4.0, BUN 17, Cr 0.9, glucose 132.
Discharge Medications:
azithromycin 500 mg PO daily - 2 more doses to complete course
amlodipine 5 mg PO daily
lisinopril 20 mg PO daily
metformin 500 mg PO BID
tamsulosin 0.4 mg PO qHS
acetaminophen 500-650 mg PO q6h PRN pain
guaifenesin 400 mg PO q6h PRN cough
Discharge Instructions:
Finish all antibiotic doses. Use incentive spirometer 10 times per hour while awake for 1 week.
Walk indoors several times daily; expect fatigue to improve over 2-4 weeks.
Return to ED for fever above 38.3 C, worsening shortness of breath, chest pain, or inability to keep fluids down.
Follow-up with primary care in 5-7 days for exam and repeat basic metabolic panel.
Repeat chest x-ray in 6-8 weeks to confirm clearance of infiltrate and effusion, given smoking history.
Pneumococcal and influenza vaccination to be addressed at follow-up visit.
Condition at discharge: stable, improved. Discharged home with wife, ambulatory.
